newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July housing completions rose 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July housing completions rose 1.1 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
The July level of 1.429 million units was the highest since 1.442 million in March 1995, the department said.

Completions of single-family homes fell 0.4 percent in July after June was revised to a 0.2 percent gain, and July revised to a 4.4 percent increase. Previously, the department said single-family completions fell 0.7 percent in June and rose 3.3 percent in May.

July multi-family unit completions rose 7.2 percent after a revised 1.0 percent rise in June and revised 4.0 percent increase in May. June was revised from a 4.9 percent rise and May from a 2.5 percent increase.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in July to 124,200 units from 124,500 units in June, but were up from 114,600 units in May. In July last year, actual completions were reported at 115,500.

Privately-owned housing units under construction fell to a seasonally adjusted 829,000 in July from 832,000 in June, but were up from 826,000 units in May. They compare with 762,000 units under construction in July last year.
